Permutation variable importance for survival models

Source: R/compute_varimp.R
compute_varimp.Rd

Estimates feature importance by measuring the change in a survival metric after permuting each feature.

Usage

compute_varimp(
  model,
  times,
  metric = "ibs",
  n_repetitions = 10,
  seed = NULL,
  subset = NULL,
  importance_type = c("delta", "mean")
)

Arguments

model

An mlsurv_model-like object with fields data, formula, and learner.

times

Numeric vector of evaluation times.

metric

Character string, e.g. "ibs" or "cindex".

n_repetitions

Integer; number of permutations per feature.

seed

Optional integer seed for reproducibility.

subset

Optional row indices or logical vector to subset model$data.

importance_type

One of "delta" (default) or "mean"; see Details.

Value

A data.frame with columns:

  • feature: feature name,

  • importance: importance value (change in metric),

  • importance_05, importance_95: 5th/95th percentile of the per-repetition values used to compute importance,

  • scaled_importance: percent-scaled importance (see Details).

The full per-repetition values (one row per feature per repetition, columns feature, repetition, value, scaled_value) are attached as the "raw_scores" attribute, used by plot_varimp() to draw boxplots instead of a single point per feature.

Details

For each feature, rows are permuted n_repetitions times, predictions are recomputed, and the chosen metric is compared to the baseline (unpermuted) value. The scaled_importance rescales values to sum to 100%.

Examples

# \donttest{
mod <- fit_coxph(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype, data = veteran)
imp <- compute_varimp(
  model = mod,
  times = 80,
  metric = "brier",
  n_repetitions = 3,
  seed = 1,
  subset = 40
)
head(imp)
#> # basetable: 6 x 5
#>    feature importance importance_05 importance_95 scaled_importance
#> 1    karno 0.10133333        0.0762        0.1239        100.000000
#> 2 celltype 0.04566667        0.0152        0.0710         45.065789
#> 3      age 0.00200000        0.0011        0.0029          1.973684
#> 4      trt 0.00000000        0.0000        0.0000          0.000000
#> 5 diagtime 0.00000000        0.0000        0.0000          0.000000
#> 6    prior 0.00000000        0.0000        0.0000          0.000000
# }
